newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MARADONA LEAVES HOSPITAL AFTER BLOOD PRESSURE CHECKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARADONA LEAVES HOSPITAL AFTER BLOOD PRESSURE CHECKS.

text.p: Diego Maradona, picked to play for the Rest of the World against Europe in Barcelona on April 27, left an exclusive Buenos Aires hospital on Tuesday after five days of checks for high blood pressure.
Earlier last week Maradona was admitted to a Santiago hospital after breaking out in a cold sweat on a Chilean television chat show where he danced a tango with a former Miss Universe.
Argentina's former World Cup-winning captain said from his sickbed on Friday that his past drug problems had nothing to do with his condition.
Despite more than 20 World Cup qualifiers scheduled for Wednesday April 30, there should be a good number of big names on show at the Olympic stadium.

Didier Roustan, secretary-general of the International Professional Footballers' Union (AIFP) which is organising the match said Manchester United's French captain Eric Cantona, an AIFP founder member along with Maradona, will play for Europe as well as Chelsea's Gianluca Vialli and Sampdoria skipper Roberto Mancini, who do not figure in Italy's plans.

With neither France nor Portugal playing internationals on April 30, Laurent Blanc and Vitor Baia of Barcelona and Sampdoria's Christian Karembeu will also play. Thomas Berthold, a World Cup winner for West Germany in 1990, has also been named.
Among the South Americans who could play for the Rest of the World is Colombia's colourful goalkeeper Rene Higuita.
"It depends whether he is picked (for Colombia) after two poor matches by the present goalkeeper (Farid Mondragon)," Roustan said. Colombia are at home to Peru on April 30.

Roustan also named Uruguayans Gustavo Poyet of Real Zaragoza and veteran Ruben Sosa of Logrones, Brazilian Elber of Stuttgart and possibly Argentine World Cup winger Claudio Caniggia, who is currently without a club.

The AIFP is also trying to organise another match, possibly in Brussels, in benefit of Belgian Jean-Marc Bosman, whose case in the European Court of Justice brought about the end of quotas on foreign players in Europe. They have yet to fix the date and venue.
